text:
elaine: Heads-up: overnight we saw a cascade where cloud auth token refreshes hit vendor rate limits in us-west2, which then caused model-registry refresh failures and a small spike in 5xx for hosted inference. Opening follow-up thread for postmortem actions.

sam: saw the telemetry. quick summary of customer impact? any Dedicated tenants affected? :eyes:

elaine: Impact summary: ~2.7% 5xx across the API for ~45 minutes, brief latency increase for four Dedicated tenants. No persisted data loss. Chain: vendor auth 429s -> registry client retries -> model-registry timeouts -> downstream 500s.

priya: on initial investigation vendor changed a rate-limit key in a service rollout; they returned 429s on token introspect calls. Vendor says it was an accidental policy push. We're validating whether it was config drift or a bad rollout rule.

jon: looked at traces across past year and this matches the "token-storm" recurrence (sudden spike in token ops followed by cascading timeouts). This is a pattern, not a one-off. We should treat it as a recurring incident class.

marta: added customer-impact notes to the tracker. CS logged one support ticket for retriable failures, no escalations to SEs yet.

elaine: Proposed remediation actions and owners: 
- Short term (HIGH): increase local token cache TTL for model-registry clients and add jittered backoff (PR: bump from 30s -> 5m). Owner: priya. Target: EOD+1.
- Mid term (MED): implement token circuit-breaker + fallback token provider (options: local minting proxy, vendor backup key, or short-lived static cached token) behind a feature flag. Owner: sam. Target: 2w.
- Vendor (HIGH): request SLA credit, dedicated rate-limited key, and a written postmortem from vendor. Owner: marta. Target: 72h.
- Runbook (MED): detection rule for auth 429 "token-storm" signature + automated mitigation steps and explicit non-critical-read failover. Owner: jon. Target: 4 days.

priya: I can do the short-term fix. I'll open a small PR to bump the token cache TTL, add jittered exponential backoff, and emit a cache-hit metric. ETA: tomorrow EOD.

sam: I'll design the circuit-breaker and prototype a fallback token provider. Need to evaluate latency/cost: local minting means KMS usage, vendor backup key needs contractual work, static token is simplest but security tradeoffs. Recommend feature-flag rollout. ETA: 2 weeks.

marta: opening vendor ticket now, requesting root-cause writeup and quota correction and asking for a dedicated auth key for Redwood. Also drafting customer comms template. ETA: 72h for vendor response plus 1 business day for comms draft.

ops-bot: Logged actions to tracker INC-2026: https://tracker.internal/INC-2026 (items: TOKEN-CACHE-295, CIRCUIT-297, VENDOR-300, RUNBOOK-298).

jon: I'll add the runbook change and the detection rule for auth 429 bursts; include thresholds, alert bindings, and automated mitigation play. Draft ETA: 4 days.

elaine: Also proposing a short-term resilience retrospective: weekly 30-min check-ins for next 4 weeks then monthly. @sam can you schedule and include eng-sre, eng-platform, infra, and customer-success?

sam: will schedule weekly for 4 weeks and send invites.

priya: I'll add a canary test in staging that simulates token throttling to validate cache/backoff behavior and the circuit-breaker once available.

marta: I'll prepare the external-facing status/update template in case CS needs it.

elaine: Recap of owners and deadlines: 
- priya: token cache TTL + jitter PR — due 2945086400
- sam: circuit-breaker design + feature-flag rollout plan — due 2946163200
- jon: runbook + detection rule — due 2945073600
- marta: vendor ticket + comms template — due 2945012400
We'll reconvene Friday EOD for a status check and update INC-2026. Treat recurrence as a trend on the resilience board and prioritize vendor hardening in the next sprint. :thumbsup:

priya: ack, starting work.

sam: ack.

jon: ack, will draft runbook edits.

marta: ack, vendor ticket opened (#VND-712).

elaine: Thanks all. Closing thread for now; will reopen as updates come in.
